text: Order took 95 minutes in the rain and my coffee arrived stone cold. The rider was apologetic, but this is the third late delivery in a row.
Fries arrived like wet cardboard, the paper bag had soaked through in the rain and split open on my doorstep.
Barish mein ek espresso ke liye 20 minute wait. Cab miss ho gayi. Counter pe kisi ne upar dekha bhi nahi.
The kids' drinks never matched the order - one came melted and warm, the other missing entirely. Rain delay I understand, wrong items I don't.
My usual cup was burnt and barely warm, and this on a wet Monday when brew is my one comfort. Very off day.
Rainy evening, they dimmed half the lights and asked us to leave at nine though they close at ten. Felt pushed out into the storm.
Croissant was squashed flat in a soggy bag and the icing had glued itself to the paper. Unsalvageable.
Ordered fourteen items for the team before a client call; four chais missing, delivered fifty minutes late in the rain. Embarrassing.
Queue barely moved on a rainy morning. Fifteen minutes for a takeaway cup is absurd. V slow.
Walked in soaked, asked for a towel or even a napkin, got a shrug. The filter coffee itself was honestly decent.
Dinner arrived cold and clumped after a seventy-minute wait in the rain. For that price I expect food, not a cold brick.
Matcha manga tha, aaya koi milky drink jo bilkul matcha nahi tha. Cup aadha khali aur bag mein leak ho gaya.
With two hungry kids and rain outside we waited forty minutes for a simple order. When I asked, the counter said it will come when it comes.
Aadhi khali cafe stormy dopahar mein, phir bhi har das minute table clear karne aa gaye. Rainy-day refuge ye bilkul nahi hai.
Chai in a kulhad is a lovely idea; chai arriving lukewarm after an hour in the rain is not.
Wet morning rush, one person on the espresso machine, and my flat white still came out watery. Maybe better luck next visit.
Croissant tasted a day old, chewy not flaky. For 180 rupees on a gloomy morning I expect the fresh batch.
Dessert travelled badly - steamed soft inside its own box, berries slid to one corner. The rain made everything worse.
Half the team's order right, half late; two lattes swapped for extra sandwiches. Monsoon chaos in the kitchen, I guess.
pakka rain day but har table full tha aur meri chai ki price meri bus pass se zyada. Vibe accha, wallet nahi.
Grabbed a coffee to go in the downpour; the lid was not sealed and it dribbled down my sleeve. The drink itself was fine.
Sides arrived cold and the kids' dessert was missing its topping entirely. Rainy-night treat ended in tears.
Dripping umbrellas everywhere, floor slippery, no towel at the door, and my drink took twenty-five minutes. Not the cosy escape I hoped for.
The board said now brewing; the reality was now waiting. Stood dripping in a line of ten for one espresso.
Rider ne 80 minute liye; cheese toast ka cheese rubber jaisa jam chuka tha. Bilkul cold, bilkul sad.
Wanted to love the rainy-window seat but the rose latte tasted of plain warm milk and the floor near us was muddy.
barish mein fries ke liye 20 min wait, aur phir bhi portion chhota. 160 ka fries itna mehnga kyun bhai?
Eight cappuccinos for the office, carried through the rain - two lids popped and soaked the cardboard tray. The labels were right, at least.
Filter coffee was thin today, the decoction tasted rushed. Zoya was sweet as always but the cup let me down.
Dessert arrived tilted and sweating in the humidity; the glaze had smeared across the box. Taste survived, barely.
Long rainy-morning queue but the cappuccino was properly made once it finally landed. Seven out of ten for patience.
Forty minutes late because of the downpour, but the flat white was still warmish and well pulled. Mixed bag overall.
Rainy day so every seat was full and loud, but chai plus fries under 300 for two people is still an okay deal.
Coffee as reliable as ever; service was not - twenty minutes because half the staff were mopping up rainwater. Forgivable once.
Sab kuch neatly packed tha baarish ke liye, par khana aur sides dono bas lukewarm aaye. Bachcho ne khaa liya anyway.
Ducked in from the rain; gorgeous pink corner and kind staff, but the kulhad chai was more milk than masala.
The cup holder saved my drink from spilling, though it arrived warm rather than hot. Rain tax, I suppose.
Baarish ki achhi soundtrack aur plug point mila, lekin order aane mein bahut time laga aur floor gili aur muddy thi.
Twelve-item office order: right items, wrong rain timing - 45 minutes late and two muffins swapped for an extra filter coffee.
Stood in a puddle of my own making waiting at the counter; slow, but the barista apologised sincerely.
Romantic rainy-window table and a lovely waffle, but 260 plus GST stings a little on a weekday.
Monsoon delivery was predictably slow; my order survived in a sturdy box but the toasted edges had softened.
cheese toast achha tha but baarish mein bhi itni lambi queue. 260 is a bit much for a broke student honestly.
Croissant flaky as always, cold brew solid, but the rain crowd made the counter chaos - fifteen minutes for a to-go order.
Kids loved their drinks; we did not love squeezing four people around a two-seat table while it bucketed outside.
Barish mein filter coffee hotel tak mangaya; ek ghanta laga, garam nahi bas halka warm. Flavour sahi South Indian tha.
Cinnamon roll was delicious and the drizzle made the pink walls feel extra cosy, though the icing melted a bit too fast.
Stayed three hours watching the rain; nobody rushed me, but my refill took twenty minutes and the wifi flickered twice.
Ten hot drinks for a rainy Friday meeting - all arrived, but two cups were not sealed properly and leaked into the tray.
Ordered at my desk during the cloudburst; an hour wait was expected, and the cappuccino foam had collapsed though it tasted fine.
Matcha latte arrived barely warm after a wet fifty-minute ride. Good flavour, poor temperature, middling value.
The counter was swamped with wet, grumpy customers; staff stayed polite but our food took twenty-five minutes to arrive.
baarish ka mausam, pink cafe, rose milk thanda aur tasty - bas table ke liye 15 min wait karna pada.
Friendly counter, slow kitchen - the avocado toast took half an hour on a rainy afternoon. The avo itself was perfectly ripe though.
Rain on the window, flat white in hand, pink walls glowing. Only gripe - a ten-minute wait for the table.
Despite the wet rush my espresso was out in four minutes. Slightly bitter today, but the speed saved my morning.
Kulhad chai arrived hot in a rain-proof bag - impressive. A little spillage in the corner, hence not five stars.
Kabir remembered my cappuccino order even in the monsoon crowd. Foam a touch thin today, still a happy morning.
Chai plus cheese toast, rain outside, a group study table found after five minutes. Solid budget rainy-day spot.
The kids' rainy-evening order arrived warm and mostly dry; one wrapper was a bit damp but everything tasted fresh.
Worked through a whole thunderstorm here; the cold brew kept me going and nobody minded the long stay. Slightly loud near the door.
Monsoon mein Bengaluru aur ye pink cafe perfect shelter tha - garam dabarah filter coffee aur sach mein pyaare staff.
Given the rain I braced for disaster; pasta arrived in 45 minutes, box sealed tight, still properly hot. One fork missing, minor.
Picked up fifteen breakfast items in the rain; everything labelled, bagged in double kraft, only one pastry got squashed.
Rose latte on a grey day is pure therapy - floral, hot, beautifully poured. The music was slightly loud for the cosy vibe.
Rain slowed the rider by twenty minutes but the iced latte did not care - cold, strong, exactly right for a desk lunch.
barish mein delivery bhi fries crunchy aur garam laayi, 160 mein kaafi bada portion. Bas thoda late aaya.
Soaked kids, zero complaints from the staff; they pushed two tables together for us. The strawberry shake was a hit, fries vanished.
Usual flat white to go; even with wet shoes everywhere the queue moved in six minutes. Consistent as ever, minor foam slump.
Dessert survived a rainy ride surprisingly well - edges still crisp-ish, nothing spilled. Would be perfect straight off the counter.
Stormy shaam, plug wali table, rose milk ke saath kaam. Staff ne geele bag ke liye towel bhi offer kiya. Sweet touch.
Ducked in for a croissant while the rain eased - still flaky from the morning bake, warm staff, only a small queue delay.
Cheesecake baarish mein deliver hua aur glaze abhi bhi glossy thi; box ka kona dented par slice bilkul safe. Creamy heaven.
Ten sandwiches and four drinks for a rainy sprint review - all correct, all labelled, forty minutes door to door.
A dabarah of proper filter coffee fixed the rainy-platform mood, served fast even with a line of dripping umbrellas.
Kulhad chai for 140, thunderstorm outside, three friends one table - cheap warmth, slightly loud room, zero regrets.
Delivered for movie night: fries still crunchy after a wet ride, hot chocolate steaming. The app said an hour, it came in forty minutes.
Meera pulled a perfect espresso while the rain hammered the awning. Prices have crept up a touch, but so has the warmth.
Matcha reached in forty minutes despite sheets of rain; still warm, whisked smooth. Docking one star for the soaked outer bag.
Perfect hideout during a sudden downpour - got the corner table, refills came in decent time, and nobody hovered.
First monsoon morning in Bengaluru, locals pointed me to brew - masala chai in a kulhad and a flaky croissant fixed the jet lag.
Rain slowed the order but an iced latte is rain-proof anyway; arrived chilled and the hostel study session was saved. Slightly diluted though.
Drizzle dekhte hue warm cinnamon roll aur melting cream cheese icing - pure cosy. Counter ke paas thodi bheed thi bas.
Dinner during the storm: arrived hot, box taped shut, cheese still melty. The portion felt a touch small for the price.
Five minutes door to cup on a soaking Tuesday. Cappuccino marginally cooler than ideal but honestly impressive speed.
Grabbed eight coffees between rain spells; order accurate, cups bagged upright, one sleeve missing. Team happy.
Monsoon perfection: window seat, rain drumming, and the silkiest flat white in Indiranagar. brew at its absolute best.
In and out in three minutes on a flooded morning. Espresso pulled beautifully. This counter crew is a machine.
Hot chocolate arrived genuinely hot in the middle of a downpour, marshmallows intact, bag dry. Delivery magic.
Walked in drenched; Zoya had a table napkin ready and my cappuccino was already being poured. Home away from home.
140 rupaye ki kulhad chai aur baarish ki soundtrack - isse sasta sukh kahan milega. brew is love.
Baarish ne hume do ghante andar rok diya aur kisi ne mind nahi kiya - bachcho ne waffle aur shake saf kar diye. Bliss.
Four productive hours while Bengaluru flooded outside. Cold brew was chocolatey, seat dry, wifi steady. My rainy-day office.
A local insisted I try the dabarah filter coffee here during the rain - frothy, strong, unforgettable. The pink cafe is a gem.
Fries arrived crispy after a thirty-minute wet ride. How do they keep the peri-peri dust from going soggy? Sorcery.
Sixteen-item rainy-morning order: every cup labelled, every pastry separate, delivered before the 9 am standup. Flawless.
Cheesecake delivered through the drizzle; box neat, glaze glossy, first bite was burnt-basque perfection.
Seven minutes before my train - flat white in hand and out the door. brew's morning crew understands urgency.
chai aur fries 300 ke andar, baarish mein quick pickup bhi. Best student deal in Indiranagar, no debate.
Rainy Sunday lunch delivered: khana garam, dessert safe, bachcho ke naam boxes pe likhe the. Extra napkins bhi aaye.
Croissant still warm from the 6 am bake, grabbed on my wet walk to work. Kabir even threw in a stay-dry smile. Tiny joys.
Stormy afternoon; they let me nurse a latte and a rose milk for three hours at the corner plug table. Grateful.
Ordered to my guesthouse mid-cloudburst; the paneer tikka sandwich arrived hot and minty-fresh in thirty-five minutes. Bengaluru wins.
Pink walls, rain-streaked glass, a rose latte with an actual petal on top, the split-flap board flipping behind. Cinema.
Cold brew delivered during a thunderstorm in under thirty minutes, still icy. Honestly faster than my own commute today.
cheese toast bilkul Bombay style, cheese bubble ho raha tha. Rainy evening ke liye perfect, aur budget friendly bhi.
Delivered between rain spells - drinks sealed tight, snacks in a ventilated box so nothing steamed. The kids approved loudly.
Kulhad chai delivered hot in the rain - they wrapped the clay cup so it would not sweat through the bag. Thoughtful.
Espresso perfect as always, and Dev warmed my muffin without being asked on the wettest morning of the month.
Pre-ordered twelve coffees and pastries for a wet-weather brainstorm; labelled by name and ready on time. Admin life made easy.
Rainy brunch sahi se - crispy waffle, maple pooling in the squares, khidki pe baarish. Kisi ne jaane ko nahi bola.
Grabbed a filter coffee at 8:15 in horizontal rain; thirty seconds at the counter and a hot cup in hand. Flawless.
Strawberry shake hostel tak thick aur cold pahuncha despite the storm. Thoda pricey but totally worth it tonight.
Wet socks, cold kids, warm welcome - they dried our chair and brought extra marshmallows for the hot chocolate. Rainy-day heroes.
Matcha delivered to my hotel in the drizzle; still frothy, lid sealed, and the kraft bag with the pink stamp is adorable.
Mera monsoon office: cold brew, corner table, baarish ki awaaz, aur shaam tak full battery. brew remote workers ko samajhta hai.
Drinks upright, pastry unpolluted by steam, delivered ahead of estimate on the wettest evening this month. Bravo.
Could not step out in the flood, so brew came to me - my usual still silky, the extra shot remembered perfectly. Loyal for life.
Cinnamon rolls ki khushboo aur awning pe baarish - humne filter coffee ka second round sirf rukne ke liye manga.
Stormy shaam, office ke liye 18 items, zero errors, 45 minutes flat. Labelled bags khud five star deserve karte hain.
